# ML in the Wild, Episode 1: Can ML Detect When a KPI Dashboard Is Lying?

**SYNTHETIC DATA.** QuickBasket is a fictional 10-minute grocery delivery app in five Indian cities. Every row was generated by `make_data.py` (seeded, so you get exactly the numbers shown in the video). No real company or customer data is used.

## The decision
Every morning at 9 AM the analyst must decide: **publish the KPI dashboard, publish it with a warning, or hold it** because the data is broken.

## The journey: Data → Model → Decision → Action → Feedback
| Step | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Data | `make_data.py` | 2 years x 5 cities of daily KPIs, real events (festivals, sales, rain) and 7 kinds of broken data. Writes `data/` |
| Baseline | `01_baseline_rules.py` | One threshold per KPI tile: the alert most teams already have |
| Model | `02_isolation_forest.py` | Isolation Forest on 4 relationship features; also shows the 6-feature first try |
| Decision + Action | `03_decide_and_act.py [date]` | GREEN / AMBER / RED per city, systemic rule, plain-English reasons, writes `reports/trust_report_<date>.md` |
| Feedback | `04_feedback_loop.py` | Analyst labels, event calendar rule, champion vs challenger retrain test |
| Charts | `05_charts.py` | Every chart used in the video, in `charts/` |
| Shared logic | `kpi_guard.py` | Feature engineering, threshold baseline, the `Guard` model class |

## Run it
```bash
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate      # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
./run_all.sh            # or run the scripts one by one: python make_data.py, python 01_baseline_rules.py, ...
```
Runs in well under a minute on a laptop. Outputs land in `outputs/` (the exact text shown on screen), `charts/` and `reports/`.

## Charts and generated outputs

Chart PNGs and the generated `outputs/` and `reports/` files are not stored in this repository. Run `./run_all.sh` to rebuild every chart and on-screen number from the scripts and data in this folder.

## Results you should see (test year Nov 2025 to Oct 2026, 35 broken city-days)
| Approach | Alerts | Caught | False alarms | Missed | Precision | Recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Threshold per KPI tile | 65 | 22 | 43 | 13 | 34% | 63% |
| Isolation Forest, 6 features | 33 | 21 | 12 | 14 | 64% | 60% |
| Isolation Forest, 4 relationship features | 33 | 29 | 4 | 6 | 88% | 83% |

## Use it on your own dashboard
1. One row per segment (city, store, product line) per day.
2. A few ratios that should stay stable: conversion, order value, refund rate, anything per-unit.
3. Your business's event calendar.
4. Keep the decision rule (tiers + systemic rule) and track alert precision from analyst labels.

See `data_dictionary.md` for every column and `CHALLENGE.md` for your homework.
